# FDG7049

> DO NOT explicitly throw `ComException`, or `SEHException`, or `ExecutionEngineException`. These exceptions are to be thrown only by the CLR infrastructure.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.3.8 ComException, SEHException, and ExecutionEngineException.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA2201
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

CA2201 reports creating COMException, SEHException and ExecutionEngineException (probe with SDK 10.0.402). CA2201 also reports ExternalException, the base type of COMException and SEHException, which the text does not name; such a report is not a violation of this rule (probe with SDK 10.0.402). CA2201 has no code fix.

## From the book

> **Christopher Brumme:** If you see an `ExecutionEngineException` thrown, treat it like any other framework exception. It was thrown from a place where the CLR is not actually in an invalid state. For instance, some invalid operations in the security code throw this exception, and backward-compatibility requirements prevent us from changing the exception type.
